bands.title: Fewer of these traits
bands.summary: You related to relatively few of the autism-related experiences described in this reflection.

bands.title: Some of these traits
bands.summary: You related to some of the experiences described, which is common for many people.

bands.title: Many of these traits
bands.summary: You related to many of the experiences described. This reflection cannot screen for autism, but if these experiences resonate and affect your daily life, a qualified professional can offer a proper assessment.

support.text: If you are wondering whether you might be autistic, a specialist assessment is the only way to know. Many people also find resources written by autistic people helpful.

social_communication.low: Picking up hints, jokes and conversational cues tends to come easily to you.
social_communication.moderate: Some unspoken social cues are easy for you, while others take more effort.
social_communication.high: You often find hints, implied meanings or conversational turn-taking hard to read.
social_communication.reflect: In which conversations do you feel most at ease, and why?
social_communication.tip: It's okay to ask people to say what they mean directly. Many people appreciate clarity.

social_interaction.low: Socialising generally feels natural and not especially draining.
social_interaction.moderate: Social time is enjoyable at times but can also take effort.
social_interaction.high: Social situations often take a lot of energy or feel like they follow hidden rules.
social_interaction.reflect: What kind of social time feels good to you, and what leaves you drained?
social_interaction.tip: Plan recovery time after social events, and choose settings that suit you.

sensory.low: Sounds, lights and textures rarely bother you.
sensory.moderate: Some sensory experiences bother you in certain situations.
sensory.high: You notice sounds, lights, textures or details more intensely than others seem to.
sensory.reflect: Which environments feel most comfortable for your senses?
sensory.tip: Noise-reducing headphones or softer lighting can make busy places easier.

routines.low: You adapt easily to change and enjoy spontaneity.
routines.moderate: You like some predictability but can handle change.
routines.high: Predictability matters a lot to you, and unexpected changes can feel unsettling.
routines.reflect: Which routines help you feel most grounded?
routines.tip: When change is coming, a simple plan or visual schedule can help.

repetitive.low: Repetitive habits don't play a big role for you.
repetitive.moderate: Some repeated activities or habits bring you comfort.
repetitive.high: Repeated movements, habits, order or familiar media are an important source of comfort for you.
repetitive.reflect: Which repeated habits help you feel calm?
repetitive.tip: Comforting repetitive habits are a valid way to settle yourself.

interests.low: Your interests tend to be broad and changing.
interests.moderate: You have some interests you enjoy exploring in depth.
interests.high: You have deep, intense interests that can absorb you for hours.
interests.reflect: Which interests have stayed with you the longest?
interests.tip: Deep interests can be a real strength. Look for communities that share them.

communication.low: You are comfortable with most ways of communicating.
communication.moderate: You have some preferences about how you communicate.
communication.high: You have clear communication preferences, such as directness, written messages or time to process.
communication.reflect: Which ways of communicating feel easiest for you?
communication.tip: Let people know your preferences, for example by asking for a message instead of a call.

suggestions: Many people, autistic or not, relate to some of these experiences.
Understanding your preferences can help you shape environments that suit you.
Only a specialist assessment can identify autism. This reflection cannot.
note: Your score is the average of all 35 answers (reverse-worded questions flipped), shown on a 0–100 scale. These are MindCheck self-reflection questions. They are not validated and the score cannot indicate autism.
